A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients with favorable molecular risk (FLT3-ITD low allelic ratio and NPM1 mutations) should not undergo alloHSCT, whereas intermediate-risk patients (FLT3- ITD low allelic and NPM1 wild type or high allelic ratio) should undergo alloHSCT.
patients with mutated NMP1 and a low allelic ratio of FLT3- ITD have a favorable prognosis, while patients with wild-type NMP1 and high allelic ratio of ITD FLT3 have a poor outcome.

in patients with cytogeonetically normal AML, the NPM1 mutation and FLT3-internal tandem duplication allelic ratio are important prognostic factors, which may be used to select patients with a higher risk for relapse for post-remission therapy by alloHSCT.
